Reference: real models, what is left out, terms

How real models set it up

The figure uses 4 experts and keeps 2. Real layers have more experts, and each expert is far larger. The numbers below come from the papers named in each row.

ModelExperts in a layerExperts per tokenSource
Mixture of experts, first forma fewall of them (dense)Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan, Hinton, 1991
GShardup to 20482Lepikhin and others, 2020
Switch Transformerup to 20481Fedus, Zoph, Shazeer, 2021
Mixtral 8x7B82Jiang and others, 2024
DeepSeek-V3256, plus 1 that every token uses8DeepSeek-AI, 2024

What the figure leaves out

Left outIn a real model
The size of an expertAn expert is a network with two layers and thousands of numbers per row.
TrainingThe router and the experts learn together. Nobody sets the weights by hand.
Load balanceTraining adds a loss that spreads the tokens over the experts.
The rest of the blockThe output y is added to x. Attention runs before this layer.
Clean specialtiesThe Mixtral paper found that the router follows syntax more than topic.

Terms

TermMeaning
expertone of several small networks inside a layer
routerthe part that scores the experts for a token; also called the gate
scoreone number per expert; a bigger score means a better fit
top kkeep the k largest scores and drop the others
weightthe share of the output that one kept expert gives
denseevery expert runs for every token
sparseonly k experts run for each token
loadhow many tokens one expert gets
